punchline: An airline pitched as three dots and three arrows: Dallas, Houston, San Antonio, napkin or no napkin.
thirty_sec: Rollin King was closing a small regional airline when he and his lawyer, Herb Kelleher, talked about linking big Texas cities. The legend says a bar-napkin triangle showed it: three dots for Dallas, Houston and San Antonio, three arrows for direct flights. Dan Roam says the picture made the airline easy to sell to investors and customers, though both men later said there was no literal napkin.
